Covariate paths from another tool, as draws

Source: R/ilm_covariate_paths.R, R/zzz-iml-aliases.R
ilm_as_draws.Rd

Turns simulated paths of covariates made elsewhere into newdata's blocks of draws, marked by a .draw column, which ilm_forecast() and ilm_predict() mix over (see Covariates given as draws in ilm_predict()). The paths might come from fable's generate(), a weather ensemble, or a scenario generator. For a covariate modelled with illume, ilm_covariate_paths() draws them directly.

Usage

ilm_as_draws(paths, newdata, by, path = ".rep", values = NULL)

Arguments

paths

A data frame in long form: one row per path and row of newdata, with a path identifier, the by columns and the simulated values.

newdata

The rows to forecast.

by

The columns, in both, that identify a row of newdata, such as its series and time.

path

The column of paths that identifies a path. The default, ".rep", is the name fable's generate() uses (fpp3, section 5.5).

values

The drawn columns, as a named character vector mapping each column of newdata to its column in paths: for fable's generate(), whose simulated values are in .sim, c(x = ".sim"). By default every column of paths that is not in by or path and has the same name in newdata.

Value

newdata repeated once per path, with a .draw column and the drawn columns filled in from the paths.

Details

Every path must give a value for every row of newdata, matched on the by columns, and paths are numbered in the order they first appear. Columns of newdata that are not drawn are copied into every block.

References

Hyndman, R. J. and Athanasopoulos, G. (2021). Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition. OTexts. Section 5.5, "Distributional forecasts and prediction intervals": fable's generate() and its .rep and .sim columns (online edition, https://otexts.com/fpp3/toolbox.html#sec-prediction-intervals, read 27 October 2026).

See also

ilm_covariate_paths() for paths from an illume model; ilm_forecast(), which mixes over the blocks.

Examples

fut <- data.frame(id = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 2), t = rep(31:32, 2), x = NA)
sims <- expand.grid(t = 31:32, id = c("a", "b"), .rep = 1:3)
sims$.sim <- rnorm(nrow(sims))
ilm_as_draws(sims, fut, by = c("id", "t"), values = c(x = ".sim"))
#>    .draw id  t          x
#> 1      1  a 31 -1.3457937
#> 2      1  a 32  1.0336654
#> 3      1  b 31 -0.8117765
#> 4      1  b 32  1.8017255
#> 5      2  a 31  1.7715420
#> 6      2  a 32 -1.4546914
#> 7      2  b 31 -0.8456543
#> 8      2  b 32 -1.2504797
#> 9      3  a 31  0.6672881
#> 10     3  a 32 -1.2907697
#> 11     3  b 31 -2.0350035
#> 12     3  b 32  2.0213470
